A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same S3-GFN work. Their text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable and can be matched across revisions.

before.justification: V1 reports original grid-world simulations, sEH molecular-generation experiments, docking evaluations, constraint-adaptation tests and PMO results in Sections 4–5 and Appendix C.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experiments and adds Saturn comparisons, additional docking targets and stricter constraint-adaptation results.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 and the main RTB and contrastive losses are retained. However, v1 Appendix B.1 specifies R(x)^β, whereas v2 Section 5 and Appendix B.1 introduce exponential weighting with E(x) = -r(x). Other reward definitions remain unreconciled. The PDFs do not establish whether this changes the implemented training target or corrects its documentation.

E1.justification: Docking coverage expands from five to fifteen LIT-PCBA targets through v2 Appendix C.5/Table 7. Appendix C.6 also adds more restrictive synthesis environments with 15 and 10 available reactions beyond the existing 32-reaction scenario. The reported PMO oracle list is unchanged.

E2.justification: V2 adds Saturn as a direct comparator on sEH in Table 5 and across the PMO tasks in Table 9. This materially expands comparison with a closely related SMILES-based approach. Saturn is distinct from the retained REINVENT + RS implementation using the same prior as S3-GFN; existing reaction-based comparators remain.

E3.justification: The written reward-weighting specification changes from power tempering to an energy-based exponential form, without establishing that experiments were rerun. The new Saturn experiments replace its usual Syntheseus evaluator with the paper's shared synthesizability evaluator. Existing temperatures, training budgets and evaluation sizes remain; newly explained sEH metrics are documentation additions.

E4.justification: V2 Appendix C.6/Table 8 extends the existing realignment analysis to 15- and 10-reaction inventories, testing recovery when feasible molecules become substantially rarer. Existing auxiliary-coefficient, reward-temperature and mutated-negative ablations, along with molecular case studies, are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report means and standard deviations, generally over three independent runs. The added experiments follow this existing practice. No revised run counts, uncertainty-estimation procedures, confidence intervals or significance tests are documented.

E6.justification: V2 adds Saturn scores, ten-target docking results and stricter-adaptation results while retaining existing numerical entries. New Table 9 gives Saturn a GSK3β AUC of 0.917 versus 0.905 for S3-GFN with genetic exploration, although their aggregate scores are 13.548 and 14.255 respectively. New Table 8 reports 10-reaction positive ratios of 0.844 for S3-GFN and 0.637 for RTB + RS.

T1.justification: New Appendix D supplies a formal gradient analysis absent from v1: it derives positive-RTB gradients, contrastive score derivatives and a sufficient score-separation condition under which the auxiliary gradient diminishes. This adds mathematical support to a previously qualitative mechanism argument. The added standard evaluation-metric formulas are explanatory rather than separate theoretical advances.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central contributions: synthesizable SMILES generation through pretrained chemical priors and contrastive GFlowNet replay, competitive rewards, flexible constraint adaptation and benefits from off-policy exploration. The new experiments support these claims without materially redefining them.

C2.justification: The new Saturn discussion interprets its comparative results through positive/negative replay and genetic exploration, while acknowledging differences in pretrained priors and optimization backbones. The existing contrastive-separation explanation and limitation to in-silico validation remain.

D1.justification: V2 Appendix B.2 adds explicit sEH sampling, canonicalization, deduplication and metric-computation details. Appendix C.2 documents Saturn's code source and evaluator substitution. Conversely, v1 Table 5's mappings from the five original docking targets to PDB identifiers are removed, reducing structure-level reproducibility information.

R1.justification: V2 develops the comparison with Saturn beyond the existing citations to Guo and colleagues and adds the Syntheseus reference by Maziarz et al. The broader research positioning remains stable. The Lipinski citation changes bibliographic details for the same work rather than introducing a new research connection.

P1.justification: Selective rewrites clarify reward terminology, evaluation descriptions and synthesizability discussion. Appendix subsections are inserted and renumbered, and publication and acknowledgment text is updated. The main section order and most existing prose remain intact.

P2.justification: V2 adds tables for Saturn, additional docking targets and stricter constraints, and adds a Saturn column to the PMO table. It removes the PDB-identification table and relocates Figure 9 alongside the sEH appendix results. Existing plots and molecular illustrations largely retain their content and design.

improvement.justification: The Saturn comparisons, broader docking coverage and harder adaptation tests strengthen an already substantial empirical evaluation, while Appendix D makes the gradient argument more checkable. These gains are tempered by removal of docking-structure identifiers and unreconciled reward notation. The net improvement is supported but limited, rather than a fundamental repair of the paper.
